1  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR  Order Sheet  CRA No. 1202 of 2023  Akshay @ Bhanu Vishwakarma S/o Malu Vishwakarma Aged About 25 Years  Caste- Lohar, R/o Harradand, Uparbasti, Police Station Kunkuri, District  Jashpur (C.G.)
---- Appellant  Versus  State of Chhattisgarh Through The Station House Officer, Police Station  Kansabel, District Jashpur (C.G.)
---- Respondent (Cause Title taken from Case Information System) 19.09.2023

The appellant has been convicted under Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to imprisonment for life with fine of Rs. 100/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo 1 month additional imprisonment by judgment dated 18.04.2023 passed in Special Criminal Case under the SC ST Act No. 06/2020 by the learned Special Judge Atrocities, Jashpur, District Jashpur.
Heard Mr. Jitendra Kumar Saxena, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Mr. Wasim Miyan,
learned
Panel Lawyer for the State/respondent on IA No. 1 of 2023, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant
. It has been argued by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant has been falsely implicated in this case.
While the learned Court below has acquitted the appellant of the charges under Section 302 and 201 of the IPC, it has wrongly convicted the appellant under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC.
The police has seized the call details but in the same, there has been no call between the appellant and the deceased and solely on the basis of DNA report, the appellant cannot be convicted.

According to the medical report, forceful sexual intercourse was committed, however, it is the case of the prosecution itself that the appellant and the deceased were having love affair for the last three years, hence, there is no question of committing forceful sexual intercourse.
Further, at the time of incident, the appellant was out of the village
The appellant is in jail since 10.12.2019 and the disposal of this appeal is going to take quite long time.
Hence, his conviction and sentence may kindly be suspended and the appellant may be released on bail.

On the other hand, Mr. Wasim Miyan, learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the State/respondent opposes the bail application and submits that the deceased has been done to death by throttling Akshay @ Bhanu Vishwakarma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168624112/
1 after being subjecting her to rape.

sentences.text: The FSL report and the medical evidences indicates that the appellant was involved in the crime in question.

The learned trial Court, after appreciating the evidence on record and after examining the cross-examination of the witnesses, has rightly come to the conclusion regarding guilt of the appellant, which is just and proper.
Considering the fact that in the post-mortem report, it has been opined by the Doctor that before throttling and causing murder of the deceased, she was subjected to forceful sexual intercourse.
Further, the Doctor has also found number of injuries viz. nail marks, bruises, abrasion present over the body of the deceased.

Above all, in the DNA obtained of the vaginal slide of the deceased and the DNA obtained from the blood samples taken from the accused, both are matching, which confirms that sexual intercourse was committed by the accused himself, we deem it appropriate to reject the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail, at this stage.
Accordingly, IA No. 1/2023 stand disposed of.
Let the appeal be listed for final hearing.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (N.K.Chandravanshi) (Ramesh Sinha)
